summary: NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope has launched aboard a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket, successfully deploying the flagship observatory into orbit to advance deep-space astrophysics. In civil and international space developments, NASA announced the selection of Blue Origin to provide Mars Telecommunications Network services, while Türkiye officially signed the U.S.-led Artemis Accords. Aboard the International Space Station, two astronauts conducted the sixth all-female spacewalk to replace a docking aid and camera, as technicians mounted historic engines onto the Artemis III spacecraft. In national security news, the Pentagon awarded new contracts to boost space system manufacturing capacity amid an increasing military shift toward commercial capabilities. Concurrently, President Trump ordered a study to evaluate establishing a U.S. Space Academy, while Congress passed a short-term stopgap funding bill that temporarily puts the Department of Defense’s proposed $1.5 trillion budget request on hold. Looking ahead, readers should watch for satellite startup Helogen to conduct two in-orbit manufacturing demonstration missions planned for October.
